newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.6 pct in positive mood.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.6 pct in positive mood.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted selective gains on Monday as the market pierced resistance between the index's 65,000-65,500 levels amid positive sentiment after several failures last week, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed at 65,818.96, up 1,039.7 points, or 1.6 percent from Friday. It had gained 2.1 percent last week. Trade volume eased to 6.9 trillion lira ($77 million) from Friday's 7.6 trillion ($85 million).
Brokers said sentiment improved as tensions between Iraq and the U.S. seemed to cool after a peaceful weekend.
"The market direction seems to be slowly turning up. 67,500 resistance may be tested in coming days and then possibly 69,800," said Kutay Ultan, investment advisor at Finansbank.
"In general, this movement stems from the market's own dynamics. Prices have been very low, especially in dollar terms after the dollar's recent gains against the dollar," he added.
Brokers said fears of higher interest rates also faded after the Treasury received bids from Turkish banks for three-year foreign currency denominated bonds last week.

It will sell $1.12 billion of the bonds on September 25 in the government's first attemt of fx denominated debt plan which aims to extend the maturities and relieve the burden of heavy domestic borrowing in Turkish lira.
